$\text{Slope}=\dfrac{\text{Rise}}{\text{Run}}=\dfrac{\text{Change in }y}{\text{Change in }x}$

We can calculate the change in $x$ and change in $y$ by picking any two pairs of corresponding $x$- and $y$-values.

$\begin{array}{lrrrr}
&&\xrightarrow{+2}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow{+2}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow{+2}\,\,\,\,
\\
x
&-1
&1
&3
&5
\\
\hline
\\
y
&10
&2
&-6
&-14
\\
&&\xrightarrow[-8]{}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow[-8]{}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow[-8]{}\,\,\,\,
\end{array}$

So the slope is:

$\dfrac{\text{Change in }y}{\text{Change in }x}=\dfrac{-8}{2}=-4$
